feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platform modernization, governance, analytics, and communications operations.  
- Good credibility signals: internal progression at NACo, measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and concrete platforms/tools strengthen impact.  
- Broad but relevant skill mix: combines leadership, technical execution, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that fits senior digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Tighten bullets for impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; add more results where possible (efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/subjective; date formatting varies (“Oct.”/“Sept.”), and “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent with the rest of the CV.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding one sharper differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct outcome-oriented language: “leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and analytics for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines strategy, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search to improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”
- Use parallel structure in the second sentence; “Leads” is slightly abrupt after the first sentence.
- Standardize style: “AI-enabled search and content experiences” may be more specific than “AI-enabled user experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” and the full capability list substantially repeat the subtitle and Core Competencies section.
- Multimedia production is already well covered elsewhere; keep the intro focused on highest-value leadership themes.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scanability and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen broad items: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization”; “Editorial governance and CMS operations” instead of “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Editorial governance and CMS operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- Standardize style: use either “and” throughout or “&” throughout; avoid mixing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level and not repeat exact phrasing.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also closely mirrors the dedicated Topline Skills and Technical + IT sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes, scope, or technologies will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/led X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Increase specificity where possible: name audience, scale, platform, or business purpose (for example, legislative users, Drupal 10 campaign site, conference activation).
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing similarly unique projects here.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Make it sharper, more outcome-oriented, and use this entry to show current scope plus 2–3 concrete wins.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + remit in one line: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on distinct impact areas: digital systems/workflows, Drupal campaign builds, enterprise web/CMS improvements, cross-channel governance, AI-enabled search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search accuracy/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and anniversary/campaign work already appear in Recent Projects—keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics language also overlaps with the summary and NACo role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened around 3–4 standout outcomes and framed to show progression beyond your earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate channel oversight into one impact-focused bullet and add metrics if available: email engagement, social growth, video output, team size, budget, or production savings.
- Prioritize the biggest achievements: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build. Use stronger verbs like “modernized,” “launched,” “scaled,” and “standardized.”
- Example structure:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; standardized reporting and improved decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s day-to-day channel management.
- Video-program growth may duplicate earlier bullets unless this version emphasizes studio build, scale, or leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to operational ownership and channel growth during this period, with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact if available: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-team stakeholders supported.
- Clarify systems/process contribution: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the footer project and the prior NACo role; distinguish by scale, launch, or results.
- “Improved workflows” is too close to the Director entry’s governance/publishing standards language unless you specify earlier-stage operational improvements.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating generic digital terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-signal wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial systems, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “publishing standards” to better match your recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more modern, concise tone.
- Keep this section purely capability-based; save outcomes and scale for recent experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies; rephrase here to avoid echo.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, emphasize the most marketable, recent platform strengths and group lower-priority tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and frame it as a strength area, since recent roles and projects clearly support it; WordPress appears less central in recent experience, so move it to Technical + IT only.
- Replace “technical execution” list style with grouped capabilities to sound more senior and less like a software inventory.
- If possible, add scope in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., Drupal migration of 10,000+ pages, AI search initiative) instead of trying to quantify this skills line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies.
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and Airtable are also repeated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize higher-value strategic capability over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and insight generation across GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Put strategic terms first; tools second. This better supports the seniority shown in recent roles.
- Tighten wording: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Board/executive reporting” if accurate.
- If possible, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere on the CV tied to this skill set, such as “analytics infrastructure supporting 3.5M annual page views” or “improving reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave the full tool stack to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider folding into “digital performance optimization.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior and operational, emphasizing studio/event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Tighten and elevate the list to: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations • Multimedia workflow coordination**
- If accurate, replace one generic term with a stronger scope signal: **In-house studio buildout and operations** or **Recurring advocacy video programming**
- Keep this section skills-based; save tools like Premiere Pro/Audition for Technical + IT and outcomes for recent work bullets

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim here.
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by “Multimedia & Creative Tools”; focus this item on delivery/operations, not software.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too generic as written, and it duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform depth or removed to reduce repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but add level/context if space allows.
- Better rewrite: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If you want more impact, split by proficiency: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress, SharePoint (working) • Power Pages, GitHub Pages (supporting)”
- Keep platform names only; avoid repeating broader concepts like modernization here since they already appear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages is not referenced elsewhere in experience; keep only if you can support it in projects or technical work.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the most current tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Tag management • Edge/serverless scripting • CI/CD
- Replace older/basic labels with sharper phrasing: use “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript”; remove “jQuery” unless still actively used in recent projects.
- Clarify tools by function: “Google Tag Manager (tracking implementation) • Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting) • GitHub Actions (deployment automation)”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere or inline: “for Drupal builds, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” also appears in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating that exact phrase here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function to show stronger structure: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a qualifier that signals applied use, e.g. “workflow design, task orchestration, cross-team collaboration” rather than just listing apps
- Consider trimming weaker/older PM tools if they were incidental; keep the platforms most tied to recent work and systems-building

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize true automation/build tools over basic comms platforms

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a vendor list rather than a capability statement. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel-management claims.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one functional qualifier to increase value: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys (email automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp
- Keep to 3 tools max; only add another platform if it reflects recent hands-on use

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding phrases like “newsletter management” or “email strategy” here; those are already covered in recent work experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider listing it first to better align with your most relevant experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. It would be stronger if reframed around capability areas and outcomes rather than a raw tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Measurement & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI design and leadership reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing and conversion optimization • Dashboard development**
- Group tools with functions so it reads as applied expertise, not software inventory.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as **measurement strategy**, **analytics infrastructure**, or **performance reporting** to align with recent NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly repetitive with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the fuller version in one place and shortening the other.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with “leadership reporting”; use one clearer phrase, not both.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or output metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific scope/results where possible: website refresh size, number of livestreams/events supported, cadence/views of weekly video updates, or growth in output/engagement.
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize cross-channel publishing processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/content roles. Emphasize the launch and tie the coordination work more clearly to organizational outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a sharper outcome-oriented line, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content that supported program visibility and policy communications.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audiences reached.
- Keep this entry concise since later NACo roles show broader digital leadership; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; save team-building and channel ownership for later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools and only the most distinctive production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or sharpen to a tool-first list, e.g. “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream studio operations”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with a stronger, more concrete phrase like “Livestream studio operations” or “Broadcast studio production”
- Keep phrasing parallel: software names first, then concise capability labels; avoid vague wording like “creative tools”
